intro.vo: Movement three. F minor, Allegro assai vivace ma serioso. The second movement ended on an unresolved chord containing F and A flat, the first and third of F minor. This movement opens on that exact same chord. The attacca is not a transition, it is a continuation, the same sound recontextualised in a new key. What follows is a Scherzo, violent and fragmented, interrupted twice by a contrasting middle section of entirely different character. The boundary between them is not a modulation but a single note changing by a semitone. The movement ends not with a chord but with a bare unison, four instruments on a single pitch, all harmonic content stripped away.

cues.label: Attacca and attack-void texture
cues.vo_pre: The chord that ended the second movement begins this one. There is no gap, and what follows is unlike anything in the first two movements.
cues.vo_post: The same fully diminished seventh, now the opening gesture of the third movement. Then measure two is silence. Measure three resumes. Measure four is silence again. Attack and void, alternating, the tension held in the ear without release. The cello alone drives the harmony underneath, three distinct chords generated by a single stepwise ascent in the bass.

cues.label: Cello solo then relay texture
cues.vo_pre: The upper three instruments strike a chord and stop. The cello continues alone, then the quartet splits into two pairs.
cues.vo_post: Six descending semitones in the cello while the others rest. Then violins alone, then viola and cello alone, alternating measure by measure. Not a conversation , a fragmentation. The ensemble divided against itself, each pair a self-contained gesture that refuses to add up to a whole.

cues.label: Scherzo climax, violin peak and close
cues.vo_pre: The first violin begins to climb. Listen for how far it goes and what the cello does beneath it.
cues.vo_post: The violin reaches F six, the registral peak of the Scherzo, while the cello descends in the opposite direction. The two outer voices pull apart across the widest possible span, the harmonic tension written into the distance between them.

cues.label: Trio begins, single semitone pivot
cues.vo_pre: Everything is about to change. Not through a gradual modulation , through a single note moving up by a semitone.
cues.vo_post: F becomes G flat, all voices simultaneously, one half step. That is the entire boundary between the Scherzo and the Trio. The violent attack-and-silence texture disappears instantly. The first violin begins circling in continuous eighth notes while the lower voices sustain long held tones beneath. It is as if a different quartet has taken over. The key signature stays at four flats , the signature of F minor , even as the music centers on G flat. The home key never disappears from view. Its frame remains visible around a tonal world that has already moved on.

cues.label: A flat to A natural, key signature follows
cues.vo_pre: The first violin is alone. One note is about to change by a semitone, and the key signature will follow.
cues.vo_post: A flat becomes A natural. That single inflection in a solo violin line triggers the key signature change from four flats to two sharps. No cadence, no modulating passage, one note. The lower voices re-enter immediately in D major, as if the new tonal world had always been there waiting. The same Trio texture continues without interruption: sustained lower voices, the violin circling above them. Only the pitch content has shifted , and with it the entire tonal orientation of the movement.

cues.label: Diminished seventh returns, Scherzo resumes
cues.vo_pre: Listen for the chord that opened the movement. It is about to return and end the Trio.
cues.vo_post: The fully diminished seventh on B, identical in all four voices to measure one, reassembles at measure 103. It rotates the music away from D major and back toward F minor, and the Scherzo resumes at measure 104 as if no time has passed. The attack-and-void punctuation returns immediately, the silence falling exactly where it fell before. The Trio's sustained textures and gentle circularity are gone in a single measure.

cues.label: Fermata, then the wrong note
cues.vo_pre: The Scherzo has been repeating note for note. At measure 143 it diverges, and measure 145 brings the only written pause in the entire movement.
cues.vo_post: A fermata , a held suspension on all four voices, the momentum arrested. Then the Trio returns in D major and follows measure for measure exactly as before. The harmonic sequence is identical to Trio 1: D major to G major, a dominant seventh, then a clean perfect authentic cadence in D at measure 154. A listener who knows the first Trio hears structural confirmation. The repetition is not decoration , it is setup.

cues.label: Dissolution and final unison
cues.vo_pre: The key signature returns to four flats and the tempo accelerates for the last time.
cues.vo_post: The Scherzo's attack-and-silence manner drives forward without recapitulating its structure, arriving at measure 207 on F in all four voices, four different registers, a single pitch class. No chord, no third, no fifth. The movement ends by removing harmonic content entirely , not resolving the tension but eliminating the means by which tension is expressed.

outro.vo: The third movement ends on a bare unison F in four registers, all harmonic content stripped away. Not a resolution, an erasure. The violence of the Scherzo, the suspended tonal world of the Trio, the collapse of D major in the second Trio , all of it arrives at a single pitch held across four instruments. Movement four follows without pause. The quartet has been circling F minor since the first bar of the first movement, and it has not yet finished.
